# `oaap app install`

install an app package as a new instance, or redeploy an existing one.

**Root:** needs `sudo`.

## Usage

```sh
oaap app install package [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `package` | package directory or Git URL |
| `--path PATH` | package path inside the directory/repo |
| `--ref REF` | git branch/tag to install from (git sources) |
| `--name NAME` | -- |
| `--confirm` | proceed although the package widens the envelope of a PRODUCTION instance (RFC-0037) |
| `--channel CHANNEL` | channel for a NEW instance (default: production). A redeploy keeps the channel the instance has; passing this moves it, and says what that costs (one of `production`, `test`) |
| `--tenant TENANT` | tenant label for a NEW instance (default: this node's own). Ignored on a redeploy — an instance never changes tenant |
| `--bind WORD=TYPE` | resolve a 'contributes'/'consumes' entry the registry could not match on its own (oaap.data.model 0.1 §2.4) — repeatable |
| `--confirm-administer` | accept an app that asks to ADMINISTER the business authorization of its tenant: it gets a key that can create roles, collections, assignments and mappings for that tenant (oaap.core.authorization 2.10) |
| `--confirm-tun` | accept an app whose service declares tun: true -- that container gets /dev/net/tun and NET_ADMIN inside its own namespace (oaap.apps.runtime 2.23, RFC-0060) |
| `--confirm-authorization` | accept a version that REMOVES something it had declared for business authorization (oaap.core.authorization 2.2) |
